la:noun:mos.html:
mos, mōris, m.
etym. dub.; perh. root ma-, measure; cf.: maturus, matutinus; prop., a measuring or guiding rule of life; hence
,
manner, custom, way, usage, practice, fashion, wont, as determined not by the laws, but by men's will and pleasure, humor, self-will, caprice (class.; cf.: consuetudo, usus).
Lit.: opsequens oboediensque'st mori atque imperiis patris,: huncine erat aequum ex illius more, an illum ex hujus vivere?: alieno more vivendum est mihi, according to the will or humor of another, : nonne fuit levius dominae pervincere mores,: morem alicui gerere, to do the will of a person, to humor, gratify, obey him: sic decet morem geras,; : animo morem gessero,: adulescenti morem gestum oportuit,; v. gero.—
The will as a rule for action, custom, usage, practice, wont, habit: leges mori serviunt,usage, custom,: legi morique parendum est,: ibam forte Viā Sacrā, sicut meus est mos,custom, wont,: contra morem consuetudinemque civilem,: quae vero more agentur institutisque civilibus,according to usage, according to custom,: mos est hominum, ut nolint eundem pluribus rebus excellere,: ut mos est,; moris erat quondam servare, etc.,: more sinistro,by a perverted custom,.— So with ut: morem traditum a patribus, ut, etc.,: hunc morem servare, ut, etc.,: virginibus Tyriis mos est gestare pharetram,it is the custom, they are accustomed,: qui istic mos est?: mos ita rogandi,: ut mos fuit Bithyniae regibus,: moris est, it is the custom: negavit, moris esse Graecorum, ut, etc.,, § 66; : quae moris Graecorum non sint,; cf.: (aliquid) satis ex more Graecorum factum,: ut Domitiano moris erat,.—Plur.: id quoque morum Tiberii erat,: praeter civium morem,contrary to custom, to usage,: sine more, unwonted, unparalleled: facinus sine more,; so, nullo more,: supra morem: terra supra morem densa,unusually, (cf.: supra modum): perducere aliquid in morem,to make into a custom, make customary,: quod jam in morem venerat, ut, etc.,had become customary,.—
In partic., in a moral point of view, conduct, behavior; in plur., manners, morals, character; in a good or bad sense: est ita temperatis moderatisque moribus, ut summa severitas summā cum humanitate jungatur,manners,: suavissimi mores,, A, 6: boni, id. Fragm. ap. .—Prov.: corrumpunt mores bonos colloquia mala,: justi,: severi et pudici,: sanctissimi,: feri immanisque natura, Cic. Rosc.

Am. 13, 38: totam vitam, naturam moresque alicujus cognoscere,character,: eos esse M'. Curii mores, eamque probitatem, ut, etc.,; : mores disciplinamque alicujus imitari,: perditi,: praefectura morum,the supervision of the public morals,: moribus et caelum patuit,to good morals, virtue,amator meretricis mores sibi emit auro et purpurā,polite behavior, complaisance,: propitiis, si per mores nostros liceret, diis,i. e. our evil way of life,: morum quoque filius,like his father in character,: ne te ignarum fuisse dicas meorum morum, leno ego sum,i. e. my trade,: in publicis moribus,; .—

Transf.
Quality, nature, manner; mode, fashion: haec meretrix fecit, ut mos est meretricius,: mores siderum,qualities, properties,: caeli,: Carneadeo more et modo disputare,manner,: si humano modo, si usitato more peccāsset,in the usual manner,: Graeco more bibere,: apis Matinae More modoque,after the manner of, like,: Dardanius torrentis aquae vel turbinis atri More furens,: more novalium,: caeli et anni mores,, Praef. 23: omnium more,; so, ad morem actionum,: elabitur anguis in morem fluminis,like,: in hunc operis morem,: pecudum in morem,: morem vestis tenere,mode, fashion,.—
A precept, law, rule (poet. and postAug.): moresque viris et moenia ponet,precepts, laws,; cf.: pacis inponere morem,: quod moribus eorum interdici non poterat,: quid ferri duritiā pugnacius? sed cedit, et patitur mores,submits to laws, obeys, is tamed,: ut leo mores Accepit,: in morem tonsa coma, = ex more ludi,.
